topics.definition: Key-value databases store data as unique keys associated with values for fast retrieval.
Redis is an in-memory key-value database used for caching, sessions and real-time applications.
tips: Redis is extremely fast because it stores data in memory.

topics.definition: Each key uniquely identifies a value stored in the database.
TTL automatically removes data after a specified time.
tips: Use TTL for temporary data like sessions.

topics.definition: Redis supports strings, lists, sets, hashes and sorted sets.
tips: Choose the most suitable data structure.

topics.definition: Persistence saves in-memory data to disk to prevent data loss.
tips: Select a persistence strategy based on your requirements.

topics.definition: Pub/Sub enables message broadcasting between publishers and subscribers.
Design efficient keys, use TTL wisely and monitor memory usage.
